learn: Python is a high-level, readable, general-purpose language used in web development, data science, AI and education.
It is interpreted: code runs line by line without a separate compile step.
The Python community maintains thousands of free libraries.
lessons.try: List five real-world uses of Python.

learn: Write code in an editor; run it to see output.
The REPL (interactive shell) runs one line at a time for experiments.
Save files with the .py extension.
lessons.try: Write and run a program that prints your name and a fact.

learn: SyntaxError: code breaks the language rules. NameError: undefined name. TypeError: wrong type.
The traceback shows the line where the error occurred.
Read errors calmly from the bottom up.
check: Using an undefined variable gives a...
Missing a closing bracket gives a...
lessons.try: Fix five buggy programs using their error messages.

learn: Assignment: name = "Ana"; age = 16.
Variables can change type, but clear code keeps types consistent.
Constants are written in capitals by convention: MAX_SCORE = 100.
lessons.try: Create variables describing a book.

learn: int, float, str, bool; None represents "no value".
Check types with type().
Convert with int(), float(), str(), bool().
lessons.try: Experiment with converting values between types.

learn: input() returns a string; convert it for numbers.
Validate input to handle unexpected values.
Use clear prompts.
lessons.try: Write a program that asks for height in centimetres and converts it to metres.

learn: / always gives a float; // gives floor division; % gives remainder.
Order of operations: ** then * / // % then + -.
lessons.try: Write a program that converts seconds into hours, minutes and seconds.

learn: == != < > <= >= return booleans.
and, or, not combine conditions.
Short-circuit: in A and B, B isn't checked if A is False.
lessons.try: Write expressions that check if a year is a leap year.

learn: x += 1 is short for x = x + 1; also -=, *=, /=.
import math gives sqrt, pi, floor, ceil.
round(x, n) rounds to n decimal places.
lessons.try: Calculate the area of a circle using math.pi.

units.t: Decisions with if, elif and else

learn: if condition: runs indented code when True.
Conditions use comparison and logical operators.
Indentation (4 spaces) defines blocks.
check: if runs code when the condition is...
lessons.try: Write a program that checks if a number is positive.

learn: elif adds more conditions; else handles everything else.
Order matters: put the most specific conditions first.
Only one branch runs.
lessons.try: Write a program that classifies a temperature as cold, mild or hot.

learn: Conditions can be nested inside others.
Simplify nested ifs with and/or when possible.
Test every branch with different inputs.
check: Nested ifs can often be simplified with...
A condition inside a condition is...
lessons.try: Write a ticket-pricing program by age and day of the week.

learn: while condition: repeats while True.
Update variables inside to avoid infinite loops.
Use for input validation and games.
check: while loops repeat while the condition is...
lessons.try: Write a number-guessing game with a while loop.

learn: for item in sequence: visits each item.
range(start, stop, step) generates numbers (stop excluded).
enumerate() gives index and value.
lessons.try: Print a numbered list of your favourite songs.

learn: break exits; continue skips to the next iteration.
Accumulators and counters total and count.
Nested loops handle grids.
lessons.try: Print a 5 × 5 multiplication grid.

learn: def name(params): body.
Functions should do one job well.
Docstrings describe what a function does.
lessons.try: Write a function with a docstring that converts Celsius to Fahrenheit.

learn: Parameters receive arguments; return sends results back.
Default parameters: def greet(name="friend").
Functions can return multiple values as a tuple.
lessons.try: Write a function that returns both the min and max of a list.

learn: Local variables live inside functions; avoid relying on globals.
Organise code into modules and import them.
Use the standard library: random, math, datetime.
lessons.try: Create your own module of helper functions and import it.

learn: Lists are ordered, mutable collections: nums = [3, 1, 4].
Index from 0; negative indices from the end; slicing nums[1:3].
len() gives size.
lessons.try: Create a list of five cities and print the first and last.

learn: append, insert, remove, pop, sort, reverse, index, count.
sorted() returns a new list; .sort() changes the list in place.
in checks membership.
check: .pop() removes and returns the ___ item by default.
lessons.try: Build a to-do list manager with add, remove and show.

learn: Find maximum, minimum, average and totals with loops or built-ins.
Filter with list comprehensions: [x for x in nums if x > 0].
Linear search checks each item.
check: [x for x in [1, -2, 3] if x > 0] is...
lessons.try: Write a program that removes duplicates from a list.

learn: .upper(), .lower(), .strip(), .split(), .join(), .replace(), .find().
Strings are immutable.
f-strings format output: f"{price:.2f}".
lessons.try: Write a program that counts the words in a sentence.

learn: Dictionaries map keys to values: {"apple": 3}.
Access d["apple"]; use d.get("pear", 0) for a default.
Loop with for k, v in d.items().
check: d.get("pear", 0) returns ___ if pear is missing.
lessons.try: Count how many times each letter appears in a word.

learn: Tuples are immutable sequences: point = (3, 4).
Sets store unique items: set([1, 1, 2]) is {1, 2}.
Choose the right structure for the job.
lessons.try: Use a set to find common items in two lists.

learn: with open("data.txt") as f: reads a file safely and closes it.
Modes: "r" read, "w" write (overwrites), "a" append.
Read lines with f.readlines() or loop over f.
lessons.try: Write a program that saves high scores to a file.

learn: try/except handles errors without crashing.
Catch specific errors: except ValueError.
finally runs whether or not an error occurred.
lessons.try: Make an input program that handles non-numeric input gracefully.

learn: CSV files store tables as comma-separated values.
The csv module reads rows as lists or dictionaries.
Process data to calculate statistics.
lessons.try: Read a CSV of temperatures and print the average.

learn: Reproduce the bug, isolate it, fix it, test again.
Use print statements or a debugger to inspect values.
Rubber-duck debugging: explain code aloud.
lessons.try: Debug three programs with hidden logic errors.

learn: Write test cases with expected outputs.
Include normal, edge and invalid cases.
assert checks that conditions are true.
lessons.try: Write tests for your temperature converter.

learn: Plan: define the problem, users and features; sketch the design.
Build iteratively, test often, and use version control if possible.
Present the project and reflect on what you learned.
lessons.try: Build and present a project such as a quiz app, budget tracker or text adventure.
